title: A home that feels considered.
subtitle: Mineral & Walnut, refined around your life.
position: Warm ivory and mushroom, rich walnut, natural oak and neutral textiles define Mineral & Walnut. Selected warm stone enriches the kitchen and bathrooms. Bedrooms retain their original individual designs; exposed wood stairs connect the floors.
scope: MW-NR01: 24 spaces, 45 day views and 24 night views. Neutral bedrooms restored and exposed wood stairs coordinated across day/night; A/C1/E stone updates retained.

rules.title: Start with the room’s job
rules.text: Plan the walk, the seat, the light and the place to put a drink before choosing decoration. Write down the daily routine and the storage it needs.

rules.title: Give each view a hierarchy
rules.text: Choose a lead element, then supporting elements. Your TV and fireplace can read as one composition. A room can have several functional zones without every wall becoming a feature.

rules.title: Keep the materials related
rules.text: Natural oak floors, warm mineral/ivory walls, rich walnut and restrained black accents carry across the house. Repeat these materials with different proportions and silhouettes in each room.

rules.title: Vary the silhouettes
rules.text: Balance soft upholstery, rounded tables and substantial walnut storage. Use legs, plinths or floating details according to the room and practical construction needs.

rules.title: Design for daylight and evening
rules.text: Test material boards near several windows and under the intended lamps. Use sheers for softness, a separate privacy or blackout layer where needed, and controllable task and accent light.

rules.title: Leave something unfilled
rules.text: Empty wall and clear surfaces give art and architecture room to matter. Collectibles, family photos and seasonal decor belong in intentional groups, with storage for the rest.

materials.title: Walls: quiet mineral character
materials.use: Propose Roman Clay on selected dry focal surfaces, with washable warm matte paint elsewhere. Keep the application smooth and subtle in this sunlit house.
materials.detail: Price surface preparation separately. Compare a real sample of each finish with the same floor, upholstery and trim; the render does not specify a paint color.

materials.title: Limewash: an alternative finish
materials.use: Use when a softer brushed, cloudy surface is wanted. It is not an automatic protective layer over decorative paint.
materials.detail: Follow the selected system’s primer and sealer instructions. A wipeable surface is not a waterproof splash assembly; use appropriate tile/stone and substrate systems at wet zones.

materials.title: Floors: continuity with purpose
materials.use: Budget replacement natural oak in connected dry spaces and all four bedrooms, with separate rugs. Keep a single coordinated undertone through circulation and adjacent rooms.
materials.detail: Wet bathrooms, laundry needs and the gym may need different appropriate materials. Check substrate, moisture, stair levels and thresholds. Wide planks alone do not make a floor better.

materials.title: Walnut + dark accents
materials.use: Use rich walnut for selected cabinetry, consoles and the owner-suite headwall. Natural oak flooring keeps the backdrop lighter; restrained black frames and hardware provide definition.
materials.detail: Approve a shared walnut sample. Grain, veneer sequencing, edge details and hardware quality matter more than repeating the same furniture shape everywhere.

materials.title: Drapery: daylight and privacy
materials.use: Sleeping and cinema spaces: sheers plus blackout. Social rooms: sheers plus a discreet privacy shade. Working/wet areas: practical shades. See the complete 24-space schedule below.
materials.detail: Keep ivory/oatmeal textile faces and slim dark or concealed hardware. Sheers alone are used only where privacy and light-control needs are verified absent. Full closing coverage, returns and stack-back matter more than decorative side panels.

materials.title: Light: layered, quiet and serviceable
materials.use: Design target: 2700K in relaxed spaces and coordinated 3000K task areas, or compatible warm-dim systems; judge connected sightlines as a whole.
materials.detail: Aim for 90+ CRI, but also check glare, output, dimmer compatibility and flicker. Mock up the actual fixture and control. Keep LED drivers accessible and dots out of view.

materials.title: Selected stone-look porcelain · A / C1 / E
materials.use: A: pearl onyx appearance around the primary bathing areas. C1: cream quartzite appearance on kitchen worktops, backsplash and waterfall. E: pale limestone appearance behind the shared vanity and on the doorway return. Original mineral fireplace retained while its choice remains open.
materials.detail: These are porcelain appearance directions, not selected natural stone or product SKUs. Confirm physical samples, approved applications, format, layout, joints, edges and installation with the relevant fabricator. Obtain the actual cost difference before committing to the finishes.

qualifications: “Go bigger”
Choose the largest piece that still fits circulation, doors, reach and daily use. Our dining table needs a plan test before any increase.
“One focal point”
Use a clear visual hierarchy within each view or zone; a fireplace and TV can be one composition. Keep the existing TV location unless separately redesigned.
“Never mix color temperatures”
Avoid accidental mismatches within a scene. Deliberate warm-dim lamps or task layers can coexist when tested together.
“Paint is two shades darker on a full wall”
There is no reliable fixed two-shade conversion. Test large physical samples across daylight and evening conditions.
“50% strength means half as dark”
A tint formula change is not a predictable lightness conversion. Select and sample the actual proposed color.
“Satin everywhere wet; flat everywhere dry”
Choose an actual coating system for cleaning, moisture and substrate. Sheen alone does not establish durability or waterproofing.
“One antique / three repeats / 60–30–10”
Useful prompts, not quotas. Personal pieces and visual balance matter more than counting objects or percentages.
“Buy custom for a luxury result”
Custom solves a specific fit or storage problem. Use well-made retail furniture; quote stock boxes with tailored fronts where appropriate. No guaranteed saving percentage.
“Replace all ordinary finishes”
Spend where an upgrade changes comfort, function or a key view. Retention, refinishing and good installation can be the better choice.
“TV distance is a fixed diagonal multiple”
Use the chosen screen, resolution, content, viewing preference and actual seat location. Test at full size; the playbook’s multiplier is not universal.
measurements: Main circulation
Start around 36 in clear; aim for more on busy routes
Planning target, not an accessibility or code approval; include open doors and drawer positions.
Kitchen work aisles
42 in for one cook / 48 in for multiple cooks
NKBA design recommendations; measure counter/appliance fronts. Accessible layouts and local requirements may need more.
Dining circulation
Aim for 42–48 in where people pass behind seats
Check the real pulled-out chair and cabinet projection. Table-to-wall arithmetic alone is not a usable aisle.
Sofa to coffee table
Start around 14–18 in
Adjust to seat depth, knee room, reach and mobility. Do not sacrifice the main route.
Artwork
Start near 57–60 in center on an open wall
Artwork over furniture relates to the furniture and architecture; mock it up rather than forcing eye-level rules.
Rug sizing
Keep the seating group connected; allow dining chairs to stay on the rug
Use actual furniture footprints. A larger rug cannot correct an oversized table.
Bedside use
Start with 30–36 in comfortable circulation where feasible
Coordinate with bed drawers, door swings and the user’s access needs; measure nightstands against the actual mattress.
Pendents + chandeliers
Use the table/island, fixture scale and sightline
The room-length-plus-width formula is only a sketch; actual fixture instructions and clearance requirements govern.

phases.title: 01 · Resolve and sample
phases.text: Measure the house, tape furniture layouts and approve a shared material board. Resolve Bedroom 5 construction, Bedroom 2 geometry, dining clearances and nighttime privacy.
phases.spend: Pay for the survey, drawings and real samples before committing to fabrication.

phases.title: 02 · Coordinate fixed work
phases.text: Assume most finishes need replacement. Coordinate Bedroom 5 partitions, flooring, wet-room systems, electrical changes and useful walnut built-ins. Retain service locations where feasible.
phases.spend: Quote prep, materials, installation, disposal and tax separately; compare retention and replacement where realistic.

phases.title: 03 · Build the comfort layer
phases.text: Buy new furniture against an agreed schedule: beds and mattresses, seating, rugs, drapery and useful tables. Furnish the primary living and sleeping rooms first.
phases.spend: Prioritize touch points and daily comfort. Keep a contingency appropriate to the surveyed scope rather than a universal furnishing percentage.

phases.title: 04 · Collect and adjust
phases.text: Add art, plants and seasonal decoration once the core rooms work. Later purchases may be phased; they are deferred costs, not permanent savings.
phases.spend: Use movable accents for experiments. Avoid a whole-house replacement order before the first rooms work.

checks: measure
Measured plans include doors, windows, services and delivery routes.
furniture
New furniture is measured, budgeted and allocated by room before ordering.
sample
Wall, floor, wood, metal and textile samples reviewed together in daylight and evening light.
layout
Furniture taped out; doors, drawers and chairs operate without blocking key routes.
privacy
Sheer, privacy and blackout needs tested after dark.
light
Lighting layers, control compatibility, glare and service access checked.
joinery
Joinery drawings show hardware, hinges, supports, power and ventilation.
wet
Wet-zone materials and waterproofing system coordinated with installer.
budget
Quotes separate materials, prep and labor; quantities, lead times and contingency are recorded.
handoff
Finish/product schedule, sample references, drawings and open questions issued together.
seasonal: Keep the permanent background calm. Christmas can bring evergreen, deep red, silver or warm lights; Halloween can use charcoal, amber and branches. Rotate a few textiles and objects, retain clear walkways, and reserve a storage location for each seasonal set. No permanent yellow/blue requirement.

windowTreatment.recommendation: No gallery drapes; discreet privacy shade on exterior entrance glass if needed
windowTreatment.coverage: Exterior front-door glazing only, subject to measured fit. Keep internal clear-glass office/media door pairs uncovered in the gallery. High gallery glazing is reviewed separately for neighboring sightlines.
windowTreatment.why: The two-story chandelier, arch and light doors should remain the focus. Full-height curtains add bulk; street-level entrance glass may still need evening privacy.
windowTreatment.day: Entrance shade raised; gallery bright and open.
windowTreatment.night: Lower the entrance privacy shade if the street can see into the house. Keep internal gallery doors visually clear.
windowTreatment.installation: Provisional allowance for one compact door-mounted privacy solution; verify the arched glass, hardware, attachment and door swing. Do not cover inscriptions. Omit the purchase if the actual glass already provides adequate privacy.
